messages:
samir: incident-bot alert - cont-batch/kv footprint spike across us-west-2. saw ~3x kv mem growth after 2026-03-15 runtime push :fire:

incident-bot: service=runtime, severity=sev2, symptom=kv-cache-memory-surge, hosts=gpux-*-pool, first_seen=2026-03-15T09:12:30Z

maya: noticed p99 spike on text-gen routes for models with awq quant path. some hosts started OOM-killing inference workers.

jordan: correlation looks strong with the new kernel selector change (PR #4521) that prefers awq kernels for gptq/awq models when token_length > 64.

lee: customer-impact: enterprise tenant "ArcFlow" reported increased 5xxs and tail latency. Support saw ~8% 5xx rate at 09:18 UTC and multiple rate-limit escalations.

emily: stack traces show kv cache size per-request ballooning due to duplicated KV entries after cont-batch merges. continuous batching seems to be grouping incompatible cache keys when kernel path changes.

paul: quick mitigation idea: 1) throttle continuous-batch max tokens on affected hosts, 2) force kernel selector to fallback to fp16 for affected models, 3) increase kv eviction aggressiveness.

maya: agreed. patching runtime config now. applying temporary policy via control plane to us-west-2 GPU pool.

deploy-bot: POST /v1/runtime/config applied -> {"scope":"gpux-us-west-2","cont_batch_max_tokens":8,"kernel_preference":"force_fp16","kv_eviction_target_mb":512} (uid: cfg_765c)

samir: running the hotfix script now, will monitor for 10m then consider rolling to other regions. logs:

```
# sample hotfix (internal)
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/runtime/config \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -d '{"scope":"gpux-us-west-2","cont_batch_max_tokens":8,"kernel_preference":"force_fp16","kv_eviction_target_mb":512}'
```

jordan: after the config change, OOMs stopped on the sampled hosts and kv memory trend flattened within ~3min. p99 dropped from ~11.6s -> ~2.2s on affected routes.

ops-bot: metric alert resolved: kv_cache_mem_pct on gpux-us-west-2 back to normal threshold (was 86%, now 41%).

emily: root cause hypothesis: kernel selector regression allowed AWQ kernels for longer sequences where the AWQ runtime allocates larger per-request KV structures. combined with continuous-batch merging we duplicated KV frames leading to 2-4x footprint.

paul: followups we need: 1) revert selector PR or add stricter heuristic 2) add unit test for cont-batch+kernel-selector interactions 3) add a runtime circuit-breaker that rejects cont-batch merges when per-request kv > X MB 4) postmortem for customers impacted (ArcFlow)

maya: oncall handoff: @samir handing off to @jordan at 09:45 UTC. brief: hotfix applied, metrics stable, customer impacted notified and request for SSO logs sent.

samir: handing over. notes for next on-call: keep cont_batch_max_tokens at 8 until kernel selector fix lands and validated in staging. watch gpux-* kv_eviction_target_mb and p99 latencies on text-gen routes.

jordan: pinging infra to run a canary patch to force kernel_selector back to previous behavior on staging so we can validate a non-awq path for long sequences.

deploy-bot: scheduled canary rollback test in staging for 2026-03-15T10:30Z (job id: rollback-9876)

emily: customer comms draft: "We've deployed an emergency mitigation to reduce latency and stop OOMs. Root cause under investigation relates to a kernel-selection interaction with continuous batching that increased memory footprint. We'll follow up with a detailed postmortem and timeline."

lee: support update posted to ArcFlow; they requested a summary of affected requests and potential token replays — assigned to @paul to pull logs and @maya to compute token-level exposure.

paul: pulled logs for 09:10-09:25 UTC. summary: ~12k requests retried, ~850 requests returned 5xx to ArcFlow. exporting traces and KV size histograms to s3://incidents/2369123456/arcflow-extract.tgz

jordan: next steps timeline: 1) today: harden kernel selector + add cont-batch guard (PRs opened) 2) tomorrow: run staged canary, 3) within 72h: release full fix and rollback temporary control-plane policy.

samir: adding monitoring runbook items: - alert when kv mem in a pool increases >25% over 5m - add dedicated p99 alert for routes using quantized kernels - add a cont-batch merge safety check in runtime.

incident-bot: handoff note created. severity->sev2->investigating->mitigated. assigned: jordan, maya, paul.

maya: tagging postmortem placeholder: /docs/incidents/2369123456-contbatch-kv-regen (will link once written).

lee: closing notes: no SLA breach yet but customer impact significant; plan to schedule follow-up call with ArcFlow at 14:00 UTC to review mitigation and next steps.

jordan: thanks team. leaving this thread open for postmortem additions and final timeline.
